CAIT adds a CAT workbench to the DSH Web UI and Desktop. It opens from a
left-sidebar entry, keeps o

ne shared store behind the workbench and twenty agent
tools, and covers the practical path from impo

rting a source file to exporting a
translated document.

> **Tested with DSH `0.2.2-rc.1`.** CAIT uses DSH's own model routes and
> credentials; it never ask

s for an API key. The internal fallback provider is
> still called `mock`, but the UI labels it **Gl
ossary substitution (offline)**.
## Why CAIT
| **Native to DSH** | A real sidebar panel, a main workbench, DSH theme tokens, and the same store f

or humans and agents. No iframe, no separate app. |
| **TM that explains itself** | Multiple TM libr
aries, mounted-only lookup, 101% context (ICE) matches, exact / near-exact / high / medium / low fuz

zy grades, and automatic write-back on confirm. |
| **Glossary-aware editing** | Multiple term bases
, source-language filtering, inline highlighting, click-to-insert terms, and per-term case sensitivi

ty. |
| **A document workflow** | Tabs, close/reopen, recent-document cleanup, duplicate-import reus

e, and progress per document. |
| **Real format coverage** | TXT, Markdown, DOCX, EPUB, TMX, CSV, SR

T/VTT, PO, XLIFF 1.2/2.0/SDLXLIFF, HTML, JSON, XLSX, PPTX, and RTF. |
| **Agent-ready** | Twenty-one
tools share the open document and store, so an agent can translate alongside you. |
## Quick start

1. Install CAIT and open it from the **CAIT** row in the left sidebar.
2. Choose **New page**, then

drop a source file or paste text.
3. Set the source and target languages.
4. Translate the current s

egment; the right panel shows TM matches, glossary hits,
and an MT suggestion.
5. **Confirm & next**

writes the pair to the default mounted TM.
6. Export target-only, bilingual, or a format-preserving

e pair to the default mounted TM.
6. Export target-only, bilingual, or a format-preserving document.

Typing in the editor is a draft and stays in memory. Confirming a segment (or an
explicit structural

change) writes the snapshot. The open workbench polls the
Host revision every two seconds, so chang

es made by an agent appear without a
manual reload.
## Features

- **Find and replace** across source/target with a preview, one-step apply, and
undo; confirmed segm

ents return to review when their target changes.
- **Command palette** (`Ctrl/Cmd+K`) and `Ctrl/Cmd+

F` for find and replace.
- **Segment notes** for review comments, plus per-segment **draft undo/redo

**.
- **Merge, split, and lock** text segments. Merge/split are limited to TXT and
Markdown until Of

fice paragraph mapping can be written back safely.
- **Term discovery for one-off names.** Quoted te

rms, capitalized names, and
Chinese proper names that occur once are offered as candidates with evid

ence,
type, and confidence; nothing is added to the glossary automatically.
- **AI review.** The QA

tab can ask the configured DSH route for structured
suggestions, jump to a segment, and fill a sugge

stion into the draft. Agents can
call `cat_review`; neither path writes the document. Review follows

the
translation model by default, and Settings can give it a separate provider and
model.

- Each document can **inherit the global TM/glossary mounts or bind its own
libraries**, with a defa

ult write TM per document. Lookup, glossary hits, QA,
pre-translation, and confirmations all honor t

hat scope.
- **Word count and leverage analysis** reports segments, words, characters,
duplicates, I

CE/exact/fuzzy/new buckets, match rate, and leverage, with CSV and
JSON download.
- Export a **bilin

gual review DOCX** (Source/Target/Status) for reviewers who do
not use CAIT.
- Export and re-import

an **XLIFF 1.2 review package**. Re-import matches by uid,
XLIFF id, or a unique source, refuses sou

rce mismatches, and reports unmatched
segments.
- **TM maintenance** previews and confirms merge, de
duplicate, and prune actions.

- Each document can carry a **translation brief** — domain, audience, tone,
notes, do-not-translate

terms, and a style sample — which is injected into MT
prompts and readable by agents through `cat_ge

t_brief`.
- Pre-translation now sends **up to eight segments per request** with the brief
and neighb

ouring source sentences, then falls back to one segment at a time
for anything the model leaves out.

- Glossary entries can be **forbidden** (never use this rendering) or
**preferred** (must use it wh

en the source term appears), and the flags survive
CSV/JSON/TBX export and CSV import.
- QA findings

are graded **high / medium / low**, and the QA tab can jump to a
finding, copy the source, clear th

e target, or insert the required term. A
concordance tab searches every mounted TM for a word or phr

ase.
- A confirmed segment can be **unconfirmed** without deleting its text or its TM
entry; editing

a confirmed segment revokes the confirmation automatically.
- The segment rail can **clear all unco

nfirmed pre-translated targets** in one
action. A confirmation dialog states the count and the MT/TM

/auto breakdown,
and confirms that confirmed segments, manual drafts, and saved TM entries are
left

kdown,
and confirms that confirmed segments, manual drafts, and saved TM entries are
left untouched.

and the private A

PI.
- **Client** (`client/`) is plain React loaded through DSH's module loader and
rendered into `si
edit `client/*.js` and run `npm run build:client`.

## Security model

- The Host API is mounted at `/cait/api`, restricted to same-origin/trusted
requests by `ctx.connect

ion.requestRejection`.
- RPC bodies are JSON, capped at 32 MB, and return `413 BODY_TOO_LARGE` beyon

d
that.
- `clearTM` / `clearGlossary` require `params.confirm === true` in addition to
the browser t

rust check; the UI asks before sending it.
- CAIT never receives, stores, or returns an API key. DSH

credentials stay inside
the selected provider adapter.
- Persistence is one snapshot with last-writ

e-wins semantics; it is not a
multi-user journal.
